Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Body, health & movement

serious adjective

of an illness, an injury or a problem: grave, dangerous

also seriously ill, a serious illness, a serious wound, nothing serious, critical (of a condition), in a critical condition, severe (of an illness), a severe illness

classical

Cic. Cat. 1.31: hominēs aegrī morbō gravī
Liv. 21.48.4: gravis vulnere, badly wounded (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 64, 331: gravis valētūdō, a serious illness

gravis, grave

adjective, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

serious, grave, heavy (of an illness, a wound, a danger)

Of a problem or a mistake, plain magnus often does (see major).

Other words

  • graviter aegrōtāre — to be seriously ill

    phrase (aegrōtō, aegrōtāre) · classical · Cic. Off. 1.32: graviter aegrōtāre fīlius coeperit

  • perīculōsus, perīculōsa, perīculōsum — dangerous, serious (of a wound, an illness, a war)

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 14.26: vulnera (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 8.2.3: perīculōsē aegrōtāns, dangerously ill (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • ut saepe hominēs aegrī morbō gravī, cum aestū febrīque jactantur, sī aquam gelidam biberunt, prīmō relevārī videntur, deinde multō gravius vehementiusque adflīctantur

    as people with a serious illness, tossing in the heat of a fever, often seem relieved at first if they drink cold water, and are then struck down far more heavily and violentlyCic. Cat. 1.31

  • 1Perfect subjunctive with a long ī, cōnstituerīs … dīxerīs: the condition depends on the subjunctive nōn sit, and the relative clause is drawn into it (the house rule on -erīs and -eris). Ruling: Perfect subjunctive -erīs, future perfect -eris.

    sī cōnstituerīs cuipiam tē advocātum in rem praesentem esse ventūrum atque interim graviter aegrōtāre fīlius coeperit, nōn sit contrā officium nōn facere quod dīxerīs1

    if you have promised someone to come and support him on the spot, and meanwhile your son falls seriously ill, it is no breach of duty not to do what you saidCic. Off. 1.32

See also serious, ill, wound, major, severe.
